content.value_statement: Container operations in Proxmox require clear status checks, lifecycle actions, and resource planning. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through structured LXC workflows.
actual_capabilities: List containers on a specific Proxmox node.
Review container status, configuration, and resource allocation.
Coordinate start, stop, shutdown, reboot, and delete workflows.
Guide basic and advanced LXC container creation.
Plan container cloning for testing or deployment.
Support resource monitoring and placement recommendations.
limitations: Requires configured Proxmox tools or MCP access.
Does not include executable scripts or API clients.
Destructive operations still need operator confirmation.
Recommendations depend on data returned by Proxmox.

use_cases.title: Daily Container Operations
use_cases.description: Review container status, start stopped services, and confirm resource use across a node.

use_cases.title: Deployment Preparation
use_cases.description: Create or clone LXC containers with planned CPU, memory, storage, and hostname settings.

use_cases.title: Capacity Review
use_cases.description: Compare container allocations and identify candidates for tuning or redistribution across nodes.

prompt_templates.title: Check Container Inventory
prompt_templates.prompt: List containers on node <node> and summarize status, CPU, memory, and storage allocation.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect One Container
prompt_templates.prompt: Get the status and full configuration for container <id>, then flag unusual resource or state values.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Safe Clone
prompt_templates.prompt: Clone container <source_id> for testing. Recommend target settings, validation steps, and rollback checks before changes.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize Container Placement
prompt_templates.prompt: Review containers across nodes and recommend placement or resource changes for balanced CPU, memory, and storage use.

output_examples.input: List all containers on the worker node.
output_examples.output: A concise table-style summary with container IDs, names, status, CPU, memory, disk use, and notable warnings.

output_examples.input: Create a container with 2 cores and 4GB RAM.
output_examples.output: A proposed configuration, required parameters, validation checklist, and reminder to confirm storage and network settings.

output_examples.input: Find containers that need resource tuning.
output: Containers with low CPU use and oversized allocations.
Suggested changes with operational impact notes.

best_practices: Confirm node, container ID, and backup status before destructive actions.
Use graceful shutdown before immediate stop when possible.
Document hostname, purpose, owner, and resource plan for each container.
anti_patterns: Deleting containers without checking backups and attached storage.
Cloning production containers without changing identity and network settings.
Increasing resource limits without reviewing node capacity.

faq.question: Does this skill run Proxmox commands by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflows and relies on configured tools to retrieve or change Proxmox data.

faq.question: Can it create new LXC containers?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide basic or advanced creation when the required Proxmox tool access is available.

faq.question: Can it delete containers?
faq.answer: Yes, but deletion should require explicit operator confirmation and a backup check.

faq.question: Does it support container templates?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes template management and consistency planning as documented use cases.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What data does it need for optimization?
faq.answer: It needs current container status, configuration, metrics, and node capacity information.
